# Tightness of the lower bound $\alpha_=(Q_n)\ge 2^{n-2}$ for even $n$

<!-- Generated by MathResearchLab. This file is rewritten on every sync; edit the app, not this file. -->

**Status:** **False**

## Counterexample

The set
$$S = \{0, 7, 11, 13, 14, 19, 21, 22, 24, 31, 33, 34, 36, 40, 47, 48, 55, 57, 58, 60\} \subseteq V(Q_6),$$
where vertex $k$ is the 6-bit binary string of $k$, is a balanced independent set of size $20$.

**Why it disproves the conjecture.** No two elements of $S$ differ in exactly one bit, so $S$ is independent in $Q_6$. It has $10$ vertices of even weight and $10$ of odd weight, so it is balanced between the two bipartition classes. Hence $\alpha_=(Q_6) \ge 20 > 16 = 2^{6-2}$. The lower bound $\alpha_=(Q_n) \ge 2^{n-2}$ is therefore **not attained at the even value $n = 6$**, contradicting the claim that it is reached for all even $n$. This needs only the explicit set, not trust in a solver. See `computations/`.

## Statement

Original wording (verbatim from the source):

```latex
{\em The lower bound in Theorem~\ref{p:lowerBound} is reached for all even values of $n$.}
```

Normalized:

For every even integer $n\ge4$, $\alpha_=(Q_n)=2^{n-2}$, where $\alpha_=(Q_n)$ is the maximum size of an independent set of $Q_n$ containing equally many even-weight and odd-weight vertices.

Source: Feliú Sagols, Guillermo Morales-Luna, *Parity balance of the $i$-th dimension edges in Hamiltonian cycles of the hypercube*, arXiv:1009.3304, doi:10.48550/arxiv.1009.3304, p. 8, Conclusions

## Definitions

- **equi-independence number $\alpha_=(G)$**: For a bipartite graph $G$: the largest size of an independent set having half of its vertices in each bipartition class.

## Known results

- $\alpha_=(Q_n)\ge 2^{n-2}$ for all $n\ge 3$. *(Feliú Sagols, Guillermo Morales-Luna, Parity balance of the $i$-th dimension edges in Hamiltonian cycles of the hypercube, arXiv:1009.3304 (Theorem 5.2, p. 6))*
- $\alpha_=(Q_4)=4$ and $\alpha_=(Q_6)=16$, so the bound is attained for $n=4,6$. By contrast, $\alpha_=(Q_5)=10>8$ and $\alpha_=(Q_7)=40>32$. *(Feliú Sagols, Guillermo Morales-Luna, Parity balance of the $i$-th dimension edges in Hamiltonian cycles of the hypercube, arXiv:1009.3304 (Table 1, p. 7); computational; reproduced: None)*
- FALSE at $n=6$: an explicit balanced independent set of size $20$ exists in $Q_6$, so $\alpha_=(Q_6)\ge 20>16=2^{6-2}$. CP-SAT gives $\alpha_=(Q_6)=20$ exactly, but that equality is solver-dependent. *(MathResearchLab: witness from experiment 92a7b722 (research run fb71b4d5), independently re-checked; agrees with Conjectures/HypercubeSquares (alpha_=(Q_6)=20); computational; reproduced: True)*

However, a result already recorded in this app for the same source paper settles it negatively. The CP-SAT computation of alpha_=(Q_m) gives alpha_=(Q_6)=20 (solver status OPTIMAL), which exceeds 2^{6-2}=16, so the conjectured equality fails at n=6. The bound is reached at Q_4 (4=2^2) and Q_3 (2=2^1) but not at Q_5 (10>8) or Q_7 (44>32). Because the solver found an actual 20-vertex set, the value is checkable: confirm the set is independent and has 10 even-weight and 10 odd-weight vertices, and that the definition matches the paper's. Brute-force cross-checks only go up to m=4. The same recorded run's counting test fails at n=7, while the paper's Theorem 5.4 claims n<=7 from its Table 1, so the paper's table may give a smaller alpha_=(Q_6); comparing the two would settle it.
